html:
Magan was the name that the people of Mesopotamia gave to a land that sent them copper and stone, from about 2300 BCE. It is now placed in Oman and the UAE.

Inscriptions of Sargon of Akkad boast that ships from Magan docked at his capital, and his successors fought campaigns there. Copper was mined and smelted in the Hajar mountains of northern Oman, and diorite for statues came from there too. Magan also traded with Dilmun and the Indus cities.

Its people built the round tombs of the Umm an-Nar culture and the tombs at Bat. Magan is the oldest record of Oman as a seafaring and trading land.
